 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 05-01-2023 at about 8.00 a.m., the petitioner was riding her TVS Scooty bearing Reg. No.KA-01-EL-6825, from her house situated in 3rd cross, to go to ring road.

On the way, when she was opposite to House No.60/85, Sri Basaveshwara Nilaya, 1st main road, Kottigepalya, at that time suddenly a motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-KC-0111 came from Ganesha Temple, proceeding towards Magadi main road, ridden by its rider with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the TVS Scooty of the petitioner from the left side and caused the accident.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Unity Lifeline Hospital (India) Pvt.
Ltd., Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident she was working in Events Management and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Kamakshipalya Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.2 has filed its written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to file her written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of Maithri.K.N vs Annapoorna.N on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139576331/
2 motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KC-0111 and its validity as on the date of accident.

It has contended that, the alleged accident has not occurred due to negligence of rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 02-KC-0111, but the same has taken place due to negligence of the petitioner herself.
At the time of accident, the rider of the alleged offending vehicle was riding his motorcycle on Kottigepalya 1st main road, slowly, cautiously, by observing traffic rules.
The petitioner came from 3rd cross road and joined the main road, without taking care and observing movement of vehicles on main road and caused the accident.
The accident has occurred at the junction of the road, which clearly discloses that, the petitioner was more negligence in the cause of accident.
The petitioner was not holding valid licence to ride her vehicle.

Even than, the petitioner colluding with police authorities has managed to lodge a false complaint against the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KC-0111 and police took sympathy towards injured and filed a false charge-sheet against the rider of the alleged offending vehicle.

Further it is contended that, the rider of the alleged offending vehicle did not possessed driving license to ride the said vehicle and the insured being aware of the same has consciously permitted the said rider to ride his vehicle in the public place and thereby violated policy conditions.
Hence this respondent is not liable to indemnify the owner of the alleged offending vehicle.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 05-01-2023 at about 8.00 a.m., opposite to house No.60/85, Sri Basaveshwara Nilaya, Kottigepalya 1st main, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3
. What order or Award ?
6. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 21 documents as Ex.P.1 to 21.

Further, she has got examined one more witness namely Dr. R.
Shashikanth as P.W.2.
On the other hand, the respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

My findings on the above issues are as under:

REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 05-01-2023 at about 8.00 a.m., when she was riding her TVS Scooty bearing Reg. No.KA-01-EL-6825, opposite to House No.60/85, Sri Basaveshwara Nilaya, 1st main road, Kottigepalya, at that time, suddenly the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KC-0111 came from Ganesha Temple, proceedings towards Magadi main road, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life,
without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the TVS Scooty of the petitioner from the left side and caused the accident.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident she was working in Events Management and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
10. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of her oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 21 documents as Ex.P.1 to 21.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.4 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is true copy of Motor Vehicles Accident report, Ex.P.6 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.7 is true copy of MLC extract, Ex.P.8 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.9 is discharge summary, Ex.P.10 is OPD slip,
Ex.P.11 are prescriptions (total 5), Ex.P.12 are medical bills (total 34), Ex.P.13 are vehicle repair bills (total 2), Ex.P.14 is notarized copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.15 is notarized copy of R.C., Ex.P.16 is x-ray,
Ex.P.17 is OPD book, Ex.P.18 is inpatient record, Ex.P.19 is true copy of MLC intimation, Ex.P.20 is true copy of MLC register extract and Ex.P.21 is x- ray.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 8, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KC-0111 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner, on the left side.
Further it reveals that, in the said accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.6, has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KC-0111 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

12. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-KC-0111 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondents No.1, as he did not choose file his written statement and Maithri.K.N vs Annapoorna.N on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139576331/
4 contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner, as she came from 3rd cross road and joined the main road, without taking care and observing the movement of vehicles on main road and dashed against the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-KC-0111, which was proceeding on Kottigepalya 1st main road, slowly, cautiously and by observing the traffic rules.
But, the respondent No.2 have failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any oral evidence, nor it has produced any document to establish the above contentions.
Even, the respondents No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.
In circumstances, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner herself.

On the other hand,
the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KC-0111 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner, on the left side.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length

,
nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to her own rash and negligent riding or there was any contributory negligence on her part, in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 sketch and Ex.P.4 spot maahzar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place in the junction, opposite to House No.60/85, Basaveshwara Nilaya, 1st Main road,
Kottigepalya, Bengaluru, in between the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KC-0111,
which was proceeding from Ganesh Temple road towards Magadi road and the motorcycle of the petitioner, which was proceeding from 3rd cross road towards old ring road.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.
On the other hand, the respondents have not produced any rebuttal evidence to show that, the said documents are false and concocted documents.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.6 final report/charge- sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-KC-0111 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the rider or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KC-0111.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary,
Ex.P.10 OPD slip, Ex.P.16 x-ray, Ex.P.17 OPD book, Ex.P.18 in-patient record and Ex.P.21 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
She has suffered contusion head injury, multiple abrasions of both foot and fracture shaft of left femur.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
17.

Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 05-01-2023 at about 8.00 a.m., opposite House No.60/85, Sri Basaveshwara Nilaya, 1st Main road, Kottigepalya, Bengaluru,
due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-KC-0111.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KC-0111 and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained contusion head injury, multiple abrasions of both foot and fracture shaft of left femur.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life,
loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.14.
As per Ex.P.14, the date of birth of the petitioner is 03-03-1996.
The accident has taken place on 05-01-2023 at about 8.00 A.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 27 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability,

has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered contusion head injury, multiple abrasions of both foot and fracture shaft of left femur and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. open reduction internal fixation with plating and screws under GA.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 35.35% to the left leg and 12% to the whole body.

The Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary, Ex.P.10 OPD slip, Ex.P.16 x-ray, Ex.P.17 OPD book, Ex.P.18 in-patient record and Ex.P.21 x-ray also clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and for the said injuries she has undergone surgery.

Though,
the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length,
nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
He has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to her and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 05-01-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 20- 06-2025, which is after lapse of two years and five months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further he has admitted that, he is not an Orthopaedic Surgeon, he is M.D. in Forensic Medicine, the petitioner has undergone earlier surgery at the age of 8 years, the earlier injury was completely healed and thereafter the petitioner has again sustained injury on the same leg, the fracture is united with angulation, he has assessed physical disability and not a functional disability, the petitioner has difficulties in performing her day to day activities and continuing her avocation.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was working in events management and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Further, she has deposed that, due to the accidental injuries she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.

She has not produced any document to show that,
Maithri.K.N vs Annapoorna.N on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139576331/
7 before accident she was working in events management and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

sentences.text: In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2023.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,92,000/-.

b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 27 years is 17.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,92,000 X 10/100 X 17 = Rs.3,26,400/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.1,50,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 34 medical bills, as per Ex.P.12.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the bill at serial No.28 is advance receipt.
The said bills is already included in final bill.
Hence, the said bill is not taken into consideration.
The actual amount spent by the petitioner is Rs.1,24,368/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,24,368/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.,
contusion head injury, multiple abrasions of both foot and fracture shaft of left femur and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery.
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 5 days, from 05-01-2023 to 09-01-2023, in St. Martha's Hospital, Bengaluru.
She has also undergone surgery.
Further, as per P.W.2 the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and the disability suffered by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 5 days in St. Martha's Hospital, Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 5 = Rs.5,000/-
is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 5 days in St. Martha's Hospital, Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount for food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs. 800 x 5 = Rs.4,000/-
is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of No.257, Basaveshwara, Kitthanahalli,
Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru, the accident has taken place opposite House No.60/85, Sri Basaveshwara Nilaya, 1st main road, Kottigepalya, Bengaluru and she has taken treatment at St.
Martha's Hospital, Bengaluru.

Taking into consideration the distance in between the place of Maithri.K.N vs Annapoorna.N on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139576331/
8 accident and the above hospitals, compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 5 days as in-patient at St. Martha's Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by her.
She might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost her income for the said period.
Therefore, Rs.16,000 x 2 = Rs.32,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 27 years and unfortunately she has sustained contusion head injury, multiple abrasions of both foot and fracture shaft of left femur.
The evidence shows that, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants, which would costs Rs.80,000/-.

But,
admittedly the P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.
x) Vehicle repair expenses:
The petitioner has deposed that, she has expended Rs.10,000/- towards repair of her damaged vehicle.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 2 vehicle repair bills, as per Ex.P.13.
But, she has not examined the author of those documents.
Hence, the said bills are not taken into consideration.
Therefore, in such circumstances, no compensation is awarded to the petitioner towards the alleged repair of her motorcycle.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 3,26,400-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,24,368-00 3. Pain and sufferings 50,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 5,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 4,000-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 5,000-00 7. Loss of income during 32,000-00 treatment period
8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses 20,000-00

9 10.
Vehicle repair expenses NIL

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,06,768/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 is the insurer and respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-02-KC-0111.
The insurance policy bearing No.26020133226230279600, issued by the respondent No.2, in respect of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KC-0111, was valid from 23- 11-2022 to 22-11-2023.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 05-01-2023.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KC-0111 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,06,768/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.6,06,768/- (Rupees six lakh six thousand seven hundred and sixty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Earlier to the accident she was working in Events Management and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Kamakshipalya Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The petitioner was not holding valid licence to ride her vehicle.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained above injury in the road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 05-01-2023 at about 8.00 a.m., opposite to house No.60/85, Sri Basaveshwara Nilaya, Kottigepalya 1st main, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-52-KC-0111 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3
. What order or Award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
She has suffered contusion head injury, multiple abrasions of both foot and fracture shaft of left femur.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
17.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.
Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
Further, she has deposed that, due to the accidental injuries she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
The accident has taken place in the year 2023.
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.,
contusion head injury, multiple abrasions of both foot and fracture shaft of left femur and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KC-0111 the accident in question has taken place.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,06,768/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.6,06,768/- (Rupees six lakh six thousand seven hundred and sixty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
